answer: A dune can hide many lantern stands owned by one trader; counting names alone cannot reveal control. Allocate agent rewards only after each identity solves a fresh, key-bound task selected by a public randomness beacon. Require commitments before revealing the task, then audit a random sample of outputs. One lantern cannot illuminate every stand for free: a swarm must buy distinct computation for each eligible identity, and sampled failures cancel its pending rewards. This raises marginal cost without claiming to prove unique humans.
